items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: The article examines whether foundation models pretrained on natural images can outperform task‑specific models for medical image segmentation, noting limited evidence from biased comparisons.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers should know the true limits of transfer learning for medical imaging before adopting foundation models.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: The article discusses using example-based grounding in EM-DETR to create foundation detection models for medical lesion detection despite limited annotated data.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a scalable way to improve AI diagnostics with fewer labeled examples.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that treats parametric curves as learnable primitives, enabling differentiable mapping from inputs to curve points using B-splines or Legendre bases.
items.whyItMatters: It lets developers embed and optimize smooth curves directly within deep learning models for improved geometry and control.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: AutoScaffold introduces AI-guided scaffolds to enrich reinforcement learning of language models by leveraging detailed reward signals during training.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more efficient, automated training of LLMs, saving time and improving performance.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: The paper introduces Contrastive Discovery, a method for LLM agents to evaluate competing scientific hypotheses, not just a single hypothesis versus its negation.
items.whyItMatters: It enables AI to pinpoint which alternative explanations are supported, improving scientific discovery and hypothesis refinement.

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Pyrite introduces a benchmark of 1,500 protein‑ligand pose pairs to evaluate pairwise ranking of docking candidates.
items.whyItMatters: It helps improve AI models for drug‑binding predictions, speeding up discovery of effective therapeutics.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.summary: The article critiques connectome-constrained models, showing that improved performance may stem from tuning parameters rather than true wiring differences.
items.whyItMatters: It warns tech-savvy readers that model results can be misleading if not accounting for parameter tuning.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: The paper introduces Continual-ARC, a benchmark for measuring skill acquisition over a lifetime, addressing limitations of existing tests.
items.whyItMatters: It enables fair comparison of memory‑based and weight‑based continual learning methods.

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Bonbon, a foundation model trained on 3.2 trillion protein‑ligand tokens, shows zero‑shot emergent capabilities for molecular interactions.
items.whyItMatters: It could accelerate drug discovery by predicting interactions without task‑specific training.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: The article compares three evaluation frameworks for detecting failures in enterprise LLM analytics agents across complex workflows.
items.whyItMatters: Tech leaders need reliable failure detection to ensure trustworthy AI deployments.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: ReTrace converts natural-language SOPs and logged LLM agent runs into reusable, code-based workflows, eliminating per-step LLM calls.
items.whyItMatters: Reduces latency and cost for scalable business automation using LLM agents.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.summary: TimeSeek proposes a multi-task, multi-domain pretraining framework to improve time series foundation models by better adapting to complex patterns across domains.
items.whyItMatters: It offers more flexible, powerful models for diverse time‑series applications, potentially boosting accuracy and efficiency.

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. items.summary: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. items.title: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.summary: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments. items.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. items.title: C^2-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. items.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
items.summary: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. items.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
items.summary: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. items.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
items.summary: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second.
